question.prompt: Jeremy’s father drives him to school in rush hour traffic in \(20\) minutes. One day there is no traffic, so his father can drive him \(18\) miles per hour faster and gets him to school in \(12\) minutes. How far in miles is it to school?

solutions.explanation:
The speed difference is given in miles per hour, so compare how far the two speeds would carry the car in one hour.

At the rush-hour speed, one hour of driving covers
\[
60\div20=3
\]
times the distance to school. At the no-traffic speed, one hour covers
\[
60\div12=5
\]
times that same distance.

The faster speed therefore covers \(5-3=2\) additional school distances in an hour. Since it is \(18\) miles per hour faster, those two school distances total \(18\) miles. Thus the distance to school is
\[
18\div2=\boxed{9}\text{ miles},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
solutions.title: Compare one hour of driving
Use inverse speed and time ratios
